items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: Sam Rivers played with Miles Davis, he played with Dizzy Gillespie

ctx.x: Well, do you, as a trio and in the other groups you’ve played in, do you avoid playing things that are much more obvious and associated with let’s say less progressive music. For instance if Scott started playing a rhythm & blues type thing in a very particular key, would you join that or would you feel like I’m going to go another way with that, and then would Warren pick up that tempo?

Oh yeah. Most definitely. I mean the thing is we don’t abandon the history. Last night we did not do that. Because somebody else just mentioned the same thing. He said, “I was waiting for you guys to do a groove or something. You never did a groove.” For some strange reason we never — I mean every night is different for us but yeah, but the night before actually we got into a really [scats]. Yeah we definitely do. Yeah. We don’t, I mean you know if Scott starts playing “A Train” we’ll jump right into “A Train”…
Well it’s not that much different than the transition from swing music into bop then. Those guys were expanding the tradition.
